title: `GDScript::reload` leaves `reloading` as `true` when `ERR_FAIL_COND_V` macro exits early
body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in: 4.5-beta1, 4.4.1-stable, 4.3-stable, 4.2-stable

### System information

Tested OS: Ubuntu (headless server), Linux Mint

### Issue description

The function `GDScript::reload` performs the check `ERR_FAIL_COND_V(!p_keep_state && has_instances, ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE);` after setting `reloading = true;` which can exit the function early without resetting `reloading = false;` which leaves the `GDScript` object in an unreloadable state.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `GDScript` object "`script`".
2. Provide valid source code "A" to `script.source_code` and call `script.reload()`.
3. Instantiate an object "`custom_a`" with `script.new()`.
4. While `custom_a` is still valid, provide valid source code "B" to `script.source_code` and call `script.reload()`.
5. As `script`'s previously created object `custom_a` is still valid, it cannot reload and returns `ERR_ALREADY_IN_USE`, but erroneously leaves `script.reloading` as `true`.
6. `script` is now in a state where it can never be reloaded. Calling `script.reload()` again, it now returns `OK`, but does not reload the script.
  - Calling `script.new()` from this point on will still create instances from source code "A", despite `script.reload()` appearing successful.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[Minimal reproduction script in browser](https://gdscript.live/?script=Y29uc3QgU0NSSVBUX1NPVVJDRV9BIDo9IFwKCSAgImNsYXNzX25hbWUgQ3VzdG9tQSBleHRlbmRzIE5vZGVcbiIgXAoJKyAidmFyIGkgOj0gNDJcbiIKCmNvbnN0IFNDUklQVF9TT1VSQ0VfQiA6PSBcCgkgICJjbGFzc19uYW1lIEN1c3RvbUIgZXh0ZW5kcyBOb2RlXG4iIFwKCSsgInZhciBmIDo9IDMuMTRcbiIKCmZ1bmMgbWFpbigpIC0%&godot_version=4.5-beta1)

```gdscript
const SCRIPT_SOURCE_A := \
	  "class_name CustomA extends Node\n" \
	+ "var i := 42\n"

const SCRIPT_SOURCE_B := \
	  "class_name CustomB extends Node\n" \
	+ "var f := 3.14\n"

func main() -> void:
	var custom_script := GDScript.new()

	custom_script.source_code = SCRIPT_SOURCE_A
	print("Reloading SCRIPT_SOURCE_A")
	print(error_string(custom_script.reload())) # OK

	var custom_a = custom_script.new()
	print(custom_a.i) # 42
	custom_a.i = 300
	print(custom_a.i) # 300

	custom_script.source_code = SCRIPT_SOURCE_B
	print("\nReloading SCRIPT_SOURCE_B")
	# Fails because `custom_a` still lives
	print(error_string(custom_script.reload())) # Already in use

	# Calling a second time, `reloading` is still `true`,
	# so `GDScript::reload()` exits early with an `OK`
	print("\nReloading SCRIPT_SOURCE_B a second time")
	print(error_string(custom_script.reload())) # OK
	# One would assume here `custom_script` contains a valid script
	# with `SCRIPT_SOURCE_B`, but it actually is still operating
	# with `SCRIPT_SOURCE_A`
	print("custom_script.can_instantiate(): ", custom_script.can_instantiate()) # true
	var custom_b = custom_script.new()
	print("custom_b.f = ", custom_b.get(&"f")) # <null>
	print("custom_b.i = ", custom_b.get(&"i")) # 42

	custom_a.free()
	custom_b.free()

```
